text:
alex: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selector change I'm seeing a regression for qwen2.5 on some CI workloads. p50 is stable but p95 jumped ~2.3x for multilingual tests, especially CJK inputs.

maria: uhh that's bad. did the selector pick a different GEMM kernel or a fallback slow path? :thinking:

sachin: I profiled a failing run: selector chose generic int8_fallback for several layers at long seqs. local profile excerpt: `kernel=gemm_generic name=int8_fallback time_ms=23.7 ops=...` previously we used `autokernel_fast_fp16` on same layers.

kai: paste of perf log I ran:```
> model=qwen2p5
> input=zh_long_paragraphs.txt
> config: rope_scaling=linear, batch_mode=auto, kv_cache=enabled
p50=24.1ms p95=183.2ms tokens/s=560
kernel_choices: layer_10:int8_fallback layer_11:autokernel_fast_fp16 layer_12:int8_fallback
cache_hit=0.71
```

eva: interesting — cache_hit dropping to 0.71 could explain token throughput. any tokenizer differences? we had a recent tokenizer merge that changes grapheme cluster splitting for CJK which could shift prefix boundaries.

alex: yeah that's my hypothesis: token boundary shifts + autokernel heuristics cause KV cache key mismatch so cache hit drops and selector sees different seq_len dist -> picks kernels optimized for smaller batches but ends up on fallback.

maria: can you repro with a minimal script? if we can produce a tiny repro we can bisect selector heuristics.

sachin: repro steps I used:```
python tools/bench_infer.py --model qwen2p5 --tokenizer merges/updated_cjk --rope-scaling scaled --input tests/cjk_prefix_10000.txt --batcher auto --num-requests 300
```

kai: I tried toggling rope_scaling to 'none' and p95 drops back to ~90ms. So rope variant might change attention patterns and kv cache hit alignment.

eva: put a quick experiment on the cluster: disable selector heuristic that prefers int8 for small heads and force fp16 kernels. infra-bot queued the job: job/2055551234-1 submitted.

infra-bot: job/2055551234-1 started on gpu-pool-3 (G76). logs available: https://ci.internal/jobs/2055551234-1/logs

maria: if forcing fp16 fixes it then we need to tighten the selector cost model to account for KV cache hit effects. current cost model only uses flops and latency microbenchmarks, not cache-hit penalty.

sachin: agreed. quick math: when cache_hit drops 0.9->0.7, we see ~15-25% extra KV read overhead which amplifies fallback kernel penalty. I'll add a simple penalty term: effective_latency = kernel_latency + alpha*(1-cache_hit)*kv_read_cost. alpha tuned from emulation runs.

kai: also see mismatched attention/kv head dims in some qwen2p5 variants — our kernel assumes kv_head_dim == head_dim for vectorized kernel; if they differ we fall back. Need a fast check in model loader to prefer compatible kernel only when dims match.

eva: note on tokenizer: updated_cjk merges changed BPE boundaries such that some multi-byte chars split into extra tokens for certain sequences. This causes longer prefixes and different kv cache keys even for same semantic input. We should add a regression test in eng-runtime that runs representative CJK prompt set after tokenizer updates.

alex: agreed — action items: 1) sachin add cache-aware penalty to selector cost model and run perf sweep (assign sachin) 2) kai add a dimension-compatibility check early in kernel selection to avoid silent fallback 3) eva add CJK tokenization regression test in CI (small suite) 4) maria coordinate a revert path if we see production impact.

maria: I'll open a quick RFC/PR template and link the jobs.

sachin: started a local branch: `perf/kernel-selector/cache-penalty` with test harness. initial numbers look promising: p95 down from 183ms -> 96ms in my local run when forcing selector to account for cache hit. pushing soon.

kai: I'll add the kv/head-dim check patch in `runtime/kernel_chooser` — simple assert and fallback to kernel_candidates that explicitly support kv_dim!=head_dim.

eva: CI job finished: infra-bot uploaded logs. infra-bot: job/2055551234-1 finished (status=ok). summary: forced-fp16 run p95=93ms cache_hit=0.89.

alex: nice. let's keep the new selector change behind a feature flag for a day and monitor rollout metrics (p95, cache_hit, tokens/s) before fully enabling. thanks team :thumbsup:
